svg.aria-label: Diagram: three AWS features share the name block public access and answer two questions differently. On scope, Amazon S3 block public access applies to all AWS Regions globally, while block public access for EBS snapshots is a Regional setting that must be enabled in each Region, as is block public access for AMIs. On resources that are already public, S3 preserves existing policies and ACLs while two of its four settings, RestrictPublicBuckets and IgnorePublicAcls, restrict the access those policies and ACLs grant; AMIs already publicly available remain publicly available, and for snapshots the answer depends on the mode: block new sharing leaves already-shared snapshots publicly available, while block all sharing treats them as private. Crucially, block all sharing does not change the permissions of snapshots that are already publicly shared, so their attributes still indicate that they are publicly shared even though they are not publicly available, and if the setting is later disabled or changed to block new sharing those snapshots become publicly available again. None of these settings necessarily removes the underlying permission, so disabling one can restore public access if the grant remains; how much each restricts while enabled depends on the service and the settings enabled. The diagram also records the documented route around the snapshot setting: it does not prevent the public sharing of EBS-backed AMIs, and users with access to a publicly shared AMI can create volumes from its associated snapshots, so both settings are needed. It further notes that the snapshot setting does not prevent private snapshot sharing to named accounts, and that a declarative policy applies the setting across multiple Regions and accounts and removes the in-account switch.
svg.title: A block is a gate in front of a permission, not a change to it
svg.text: Three features, one name, and no shared answer to either question.
Block public access — S3, EBS snapshots, AMIs.
SCOPE — how far one call reaches
S3 “the settings apply to all AWS Regions globally”
Snapshots “a Regional setting … enable … in each Region”
AMIs must be disabled “in each Region in which the AMI will be publicly shared”
One call for S3 across the world. One call per Region for the other two — including the Regions nobody uses,
which is exactly where an unnoticed public snapshot sits.
ALREADY PUBLIC — and what the stronger mode really does
S3 policies kept, but RestrictPublicBuckets and IgnorePublicAcls restrict the access they grant
AMIs “they remain publicly available”
Snapshots block new sharing: “remain publicly available” · block all sharing: “treated as private”
But: “does not change the permissions … the attributes for these snapshots still indicate that they are
publicly shared, even though they are not publicly available.”
So the masking has a half-life
“If you later disable block public access or change
the mode to block new sharing, these snapshots will
become publicly available again.”
The attribute was telling the truth.
The documented way around it
“does not prevent the public sharing of EBS-backed
AMIs … users with access to that AMI can create
volumes from its associated snapshots.”
Enable both settings, or neither counts.
And it is not an egress control
“Block public access for snapshots does not prevent private snapshot sharing.” Named-account sharing is untouched.
None of these necessarily removes the underlying permission.
Disabling one can restore public access if the grant is still in place. How much each restricts while enabled differs by service.
